translationRepairs: s0001 列傳第四十四 is the biography serial number; the idiomatic 'year' is invented and Biography 44 matches the Chinese.
Empress Wang gave birth to the Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi and to Prince Dalian of Nankang.
Empress Wang gave birth to the Lamented Crown Prince Daqi and to Prince Dalian of Nanjun.
s0004 哀太子大器、南郡王大連: 大器 is Daqi and 南郡 is Nanjun; Dadqi and Nankang are wrong.
Empress Wang bore the Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi and Prince Dalian of Nankang.
Empress Wang bore the Lamented Crown Prince Daqi and Prince Dalian of Nanjun.
Literal of s0004 repeats Dadqi for 大器 and Nankang for 南郡; Daqi and Nanjun are correct.
Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liyang.
Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liuyang.
s0007 瀏陽公大雅: 瀏陽 is Liuyang, not Liyang (歷陽).
Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liyang.
Lady Xie bore Duke Daya of Liuyang.
Literal likewise misreads 瀏陽 as Liyang; Liuyang is the accurate place-name.
Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dadjun of Xiyang.
Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dajun of Xiyang.
s0009 西陽王大鈞: 大鈞 is Dajun; Dadjun inserts a spurious d.
Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dadjun of Xiyang.
Bao Zhaohua bore Prince Dajun of Xiyang.
Literal of s0009 has the same Dadjun error for 大鈞; Dajun is correct.
Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Dadun, who died young and received no enfeoffment.
Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Daxun, who died young and received no enfeoffment.
s0015 皇子大訓: 大訓 is Daxun, not Dadun.
Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Dadun, who died young without a fief.
Lady Pan Mei bore the imperial son Daxun, who died young without a fief.
Literal likewise misreads 大訓 as Dadun; Daxun matches the Chinese.

In the third year the Terrace City fell; Xiao Shao of the superior armor fled south with a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and given the title General Who Pacifies the South.
In the third year the Terrace City fell; Marquis Xiao Shao of Shangjia fled south with a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and given the title General Who Pacifies the South.
s0054 上甲侯蕭韶: 上甲侯 is Marquis of Shangjia, not 'superior armor'.

In the third year the Terrace City fell; the superior armor officer Xiao Shao fled south bearing a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
In the third year the Terrace City fell; Marquis Xiao Shao of Shangjia fled south bearing a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
Literal of s0054 likewise misreads 上甲侯 as a superior-armor office; Marquis of Shangjia is correct.
At first, Zhuang Tie, Administrator of Liyang, surrendered the city to Hou Jing, but afterward he brought his mother and came over to Daxin.
At first, Zhuang Tie, Administrator of Liyang, surrendered the city to Hou Jing, but afterward he brought his mother and came over as a refugee.
s0056 奉其母來奔 states only that he came fleeing/defecting; naming Daxin as destination is not in the Chinese.
Sizian, heir of Poyang, was Tie's friend and told Fan, "I used to keep company with Tie—he is clever and bold. If he surrenders to Jiangzhou they will not spare his life. Please aid him."

Si, the heir of Poyang, had previously been friendly with Tie and told Fan, "I used to keep company with Tie—he is clever and bold. If he surrenders to Jiangzhou they will not spare his life. Please aid him."
s0062 鄱陽世子嗣先與鐵善: 嗣 is the heir's name and 先 means previously; Sizian is a false compound.

The heir of Poyang, Sizian, was friendly with Tie and said to Fan, "In the past I associated with Tie; his talent and stratagems are resourceful—if he surrenders to Jiangzhou, his head will surely not be spared. Please rescue him."

The heir of Poyang, Si, was previously friendly with Tie and said to Fan, "In the past I associated with Tie; his talent and stratagems are resourceful—if he surrenders to Jiangzhou, his head will surely not be spared. Please rescue him."
Literal of s0062 likewise treats 嗣先 as one name; Si plus adverb 先 is the correct parse.
In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery, went out as Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Dongyang, and was also removed to be Prefect of Wu commandery.
In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery, went out as Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, and was also appointed Prefect of Wu commandery.
s0082 又除吳郡太守: 除 means appoint, so 'removed' is wrong; the proposal still leaves 東揚州 as Dongyang, which must be Eastern Yangzhou.
At the time Zhang Biao raised a righteous army in Kuaiji; the men of Wu, Lu Linggong and Yingchuan's Yu Mengqing, urged Dalin to join him.
At the time Zhang Biao raised a righteous army in Kuaiji; Lu Linggong of Wu and Yu Mengqing of Yingchuan urged Dalin to join him.
s0083 吳人陸令公、潁川庾孟卿: 吳人 modifies only Lu Linggong; Yingchuan labels Yu Mengqing separately.
and if he is crushed, to go because I urged it—that I will not do."
and if he is crushed and defeated, they would blame it on me—I must not go."
s0085 以我說焉 means the defeat would be explained by reference to him, not that he goes because he urged it.
Prince Dalian of Nankang, styled Renjing, was the fifth son of Emperor Jianwen.
Prince Dalian of Nanjun, styled Renjing, was the fifth son of Emperor Jianwen.
s0087 南郡王大連: 南郡 is Nanjun, not Nankang.
Prince Dalian of Nankang, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's fifth son.
Prince Dalian of Nanjun, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's fifth son.
Literal of s0087 likewise misreads 南郡 as Nankang; Nanjun is correct.
In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu and made Inspector of Dongyang.
In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu and made Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
s0108 東揚州刺史 is Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, not Dongyang.
In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu commandery and went out as Inspector of Dongyang.
In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu commandery and went out as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
Literal of s0108 likewise misreads 東揚州 as Dongyang; Eastern Yangzhou matches the Chinese.
Duke Daya of Liyang, styled Renfeng, was the twelfth son of Emperor Jianwen.
Duke Daya of Liuyang, styled Renfeng, was the twelfth son of Emperor Jianwen.
s0124 瀏陽公大雅: 瀏陽 is Liuyang; Liyang drops the medial vowel.
Duke Daya of Liyang, style name Renfeng, was Emperor Jianwen's twelfth son.
Duke Daya of Liuyang, style name Renfeng, was Emperor Jianwen's twelfth son.
Literal of s0124 has the same Liyang error for 瀏陽; Liuyang is correct.
In the ninth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang.
In the ninth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang.
s0125 封瀏陽縣公: 瀏陽 is Liuyang, not Liyang.
In the ninth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang county.
In the ninth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang county.
Literal of s0125 likewise needs Liuyang for 瀏陽.
Prince Dadjun of Xiyang, styled Renbo, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
Prince Dajun of Xiyang, styled Renbo, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
s0134 西陽王大鈞: 大鈞 is Dajun; Dadjun is wrong.
Prince Dadjun of Xiyang, style name Renbo, was Emperor Jianwen's fourteenth son.
Prince Dajun of Xiyang, style name Renbo, was Emperor Jianwen's fourteenth son.
Literal of s0134 repeats Dadjun for 大鈞; Dajun is correct.
The imperial son Dadun, styled Rende, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
The imperial son Daxun, styled Rende, was the sixteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
s0145 皇子大訓: 大訓 is Daxun, not Dadun.
The imperial son Dadun, style name Rende, was Emperor Jianwen's sixteenth son.
The imperial son Daxun, style name Rende, was Emperor Jianwen's sixteenth son.
Literal of s0145 likewise misreads 大訓 as Dadun; Daxun matches the Chinese.
He then worshiped the Buddha at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever living beings ought to receive the report of suffering, let Daqiu take it all."
He then worshiped the Buddha at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever living beings ought to receive the retribution of suffering, let Daqiu take it all."
s0153 苦報 is karmic retribution of suffering, not a 'report' of suffering.
In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master with Opens Office and Parallels in Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master Unequaled in Ceremonial with the Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
s0268 開府儀同三司 is the conventional Grand Master Unequaled in Ceremonial with the Three Departments; 'Opens Office' is a broken calque.
In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master with Opens Office and Parallels in Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master Unequaled in Ceremonial with the Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
Literal of s0268 has the same Opens Office calque for 開府儀同三司; the conventional office name is required.

The Martial and Fierce heir, with talent fit to stem disaster, held the charge of the heir in the tomb-line—yet in the end he was cast aside that same year; fortune and misfortune, too, are said to be fate. Alas!

The Martial and Fierce heir, with talent fit to manage his father's unfinished work, held the charge of the primary heir—yet in the end he was cast aside that same year; fortune and misfortune, too, are said to be fate. Alas!
s0227 幹蠱 means managing the father's unfinished work and 塚嗣 is the primary heir, not a tomb-line.
